core_obligations: Prove that the halting function h is not partial recursive, by a diagonal argument on indices
proof_roadmap: Suppose h is partial recursive and define the diagonal partial function d(y)=1 if h(y,y)=0, undefined otherwise
Read off the two clauses: d(y) is defined iff h(y,y) does not halt on input (y,y), i.e. iff cf_y(y) is undefined
If h is partial recursive then d is partial recursive, so by the Kleene normal form theorem d has an index e_d
Case h(e_d,e_d)=1: then cf_{e_d}(e_d) is defined, but d(e_d) is defined iff h(e_d,e_d)=0, contradiction
Case h(e_d,e_d)=0: then d(e_d) is undefined, again contradicting cf_{e_d} ~= d
Both cases fail, so e_d cannot index a partial recursive function while the assumed partial recursiveness of h makes the definition admissible; hence h is not partial recursive
difficulty_reason: Classic diagonalization; the argument is short and fully written out in the source, the only care needed is tracking the defined/undefined behaviour of partial functions through the two cases.
